name: Namungumi
body:
NAMUNGUMI
CR 11

The shape of what appears to be a sort of quadrupedal whale bursts forth from the lake before you. It’s eyes glint with suspicion, and it’s claws clatter against the rocks. It opens its mouth to let out a deep, musical roar, baring its rows of razor-sharp teeth.

XP 12,800
LG Gargantuan magical beast
Init -1; Senses blindsight 120 ft., low-light vision; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 5, flat-footed 13 (+8 natural, –4 size)
hp 228 (16d10+60)
Fort +14, Ref +10, Will +10
Defensive Abilities hold breath, keen hearing, ceremonial flesh
Weaknesses echolocation dependence

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.; swim 60 ft.
Melee bite +13 (4d8+9 piercing), 2 claws +13 (4d6+9 slashing), tail +13 (4d6+9 bludgeoning, double versus objects)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks swallow whole (4d8+9 plus 2d6 acid, AC 10, 25 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 28, Dex 10, Con 19, Int 13, Wis 20, Cha 13
Base Atk +16; CMB +29; CMD 39
Feats Endurance, Improved Initiative, Skill Focus (Perception, Swim), Weapon Focus (bite), Weapon Focus (claw), Weapon Focus (tail)
Skills Climb +4, Perception +16, Swim +28; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception
Languages Speaks the languages of the people living near the lake it inhabits

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ceremonial Flesh (Sp)

The flesh of a namungumi can be carved and eaten as part of a ceremony or ritual. All those present at the event who are taking part willingly can benefit. Each willing creature that eats a namungumi’s flesh as part of the ritual gains the benefits of a heroes’ feast spell. Each such creature also gains the benefits of a ceremony spell, with the effect corresponding to the sort of ritual being conducted (GM’s discretion). No creature can benefit from eating a namungumi’s flesh more than once during any given ritual (typically no more than once per season). The carving of a namungumi’s flesh during the ritual causes no harm to the namungumi, as the creature instantly regenerates the damage.

Echolocation Dependence (Ex)

A namungumi can’t use its Blindsight while deafened.

Hold Breath (Ex)

A namungumi can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 6 times its Constitution score before it risks drowning.

Keen Hearing (Ex)

A namungumi has a +5 bonus on Perception checks that rely on hearing.

ECOLOGY

Environment lakes
Organization solitary, pair, or pod (3-20)
Treasure none

Namungumi are benevolent, quadrupedal, whale-like creatures that that inhabit large lakes. They are often involved in village initiation rituals and other traditional ceremonies. The flesh of a namungumi can be harvested and has numerous mystical properties, though carving it causes no harm to the namungumi. Creatures that eat the flesh of a namungumi gain a number of benefits, though only if they are participating in a ceremony in good faith.

Namungumi are considered by some scholars to be genius loci, patron spirits or creatures of a local area—in this case, a lake. While they are herbivorous and peaceful, they can become fierce and aggressive when their “people” are threatened.

Not all namungumi are benevolent. Less commonly, certain namungumi have more of a trickster personality, sometimes tipping canoes and killing hippos. These namungumi are typically smaller than their benevolent kin, though not always. Unlike their more benevolent kin, trickster namungumi are carnivorous, and they have no qualms about eating people.
